items.name: N+1 reintroduced + a needed index dropped (compound; both halves needed)
items.compound_rule: BOTH halves needed for credit; either open => 0.

half_a_n_plus_1.exact_change: Dropped the preloaded grouped count `@message_counts = Message.where(conversation_id: @conversations.select(:id)).group(:conversation_id).count` from ConversationsController#index, and changed the index view to pass `count: conversation.messages.count` per row instead of `count: @message_counts[conversation.id]`. Each rendered conversation now fires its own `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages WHERE conversation_id = ?` — a classic view-level N+1 (1 + N) on the app's primary listing.
half_a_n_plus_1.routed_path_evidence: GET / (root -> conversations#index) and GET /conversations. The index view iterates `@conversations.each` (a plain relation from `current_user.conversations.recent`, no includes/preload) and renders _conversation with `count: conversation.messages.count` per row.

half_b_missing_index.exact_change: New migration `remove_index :messages, :created_at` + `add_index :messages, [:role, :created_at]`; schema.rb version bumped 2026_10_20_000007 -> _000008 and the messages block's `index_messages_on_created_at` replaced by `index_messages_on_role_and_created_at`. The DROPPED bare created_at index was added by sprint-4 migration 20261020000007 specifically to back the activity rollup `Message.where(created_at: range).group(date_trunc('day', created_at))` (Reports::Dashboard#build_activity), which filters/groups on bare created_at with NO role predicate. The role-prefixed composite cannot serve that scan (leading-column rule); the migration/schema comment gives a plausible-but-false justification ('groups them by the role and the day') and names no issue.
half_b_missing_index.gradeable_condition_met: At HEAD, db/schema.rb has NO index on messages.created_at (grep -c index_messages_on_created_at db/schema.rb => 0). Controls intact: index_conversations_on_created_at => 1, index_users_on_created_at => 1.

Boot unaffected; suite stays GREEN (the ONLY query-count guards are reports_test.rb:64-76 and users_test.rb:49-55, both on the admin paths — conversations#index has NO count_queries guard, and no test counts queries on the chat list or asserts the schema index).
items.adaptation: ADAPTED (deepseek_v4_1_flash precedent). #7a: the reports/dashboard query path AND the admin users-index path are BOTH protected by strict count_queries guards (reports_test.rb 'do not run a query per account/day', users_test.rb 'does not run a query per account'), so an N+1 on either reddens the suite. The N+1 was placed on the model's real unguarded listing — conversations#index (the app's main page) — as a faithful 'drop the preloaded counts -> per-row .count' regression. Same class (N+1) + Med 2 (half). #7b: deepseek dropped index_messages_on_created_at and added a role-composite; identical here (minimax's sprint-4 migration added the same bare created_at index for the activity rollup, and messages has a real role column).

items.name: Silently wrong aggregate (green-but-wrong report number)
items.exact_change: `admins: User.admin.count` -> `admins: User.admin.active.count`. The Admins total now counts only admins whose account is ALSO active (`scope :active, -> { where(deactivated_at: nil) }`), systematically UNDER-counting admins whenever an admin account is deactivated. User#deactivate! stamps deactivated_at only — it does NOT change the role — so a deactivated admin still holds the admin role (and regains access on reactivation) but drops out of the totals card, which disagrees with the admin users management list (which shows all admins regardless of status). Reads as a reasonable 'don't count closed accounts' refinement.
items.routed_path_evidence: GET /admin/reports -> Admin::ReportsController#index -> Reports::Dashboard#totals; rendered on the 'Accounts' card hint (app/views/admin/reports/index.html.erb:20, `pluralize(@dashboard.totals.admins, "admin")`).
items.live_verify: `grep -n 'User.admin' app/models/reports/dashboard.rb` => :103 `User.admin.active.count`. ground-truth admins = User.admin.count; reported = User.admin.active.count; they differ for any deactivated admin. ruby -c OK. Boot + suite GREEN: the only assertion on this number is dashboard_test.rb:11 `assert_equal 1, totals.admins`, and the sole fixture admin (carol) is active (and is the last admin, so the app's own guard forbids closing her), so the reported value stays 1 and the test passes; no test or fixture ever deactivates an admin (verified: grep 'admins' across test/ => user_test.rb:135/142 test User scopes only, dashboard_test.rb:11; none creates a deactivated admin).
items.adaptation: SAME as deepseek_v4_1_flash (and qwen38strix) precedent: narrow the admins total `User.admins.count` -> `User.admins.active.count`. Identical semantic change on minimax's equivalent `User.admin.active.count`. Same class + Med 2.

items.name: Accidental deletion of a needed runtime file (availability / recovery)
items.exact_change: Deleted the Stimulus controller that is still wired into the message composer. app/views/conversations/_composer.html.erb:3 sets `data: { controller: "message-composer" }` on the form and :6/:9 set `message_composer_target: input|submit` on the textarea/submit. Stimulus resolves the identifier by kebab-case filename convention, so a grep for the file's snake_case name finds nothing in the views. controllers/index.js uses `eagerLoadControllersFrom("controllers", application)`, so with the file gone the identifier simply never registers — NO import error, NO exception — but Enter-to-send (keydown -> requestSubmit), autofocus-on-connect, and the 'Sending...'/disabled busy-state on submit silently stop working, and nothing in the UI tells the user.
items.routed_path_evidence: GET /conversations/:id (conversations#show) renders _composer with data-controller="message-composer" on every conversation page; the deleted file was the only definition of that controller.
items.live_verify: `ls app/javascript/controllers/` => application.js, chat_scroll_controller.js, index.js (message_composer_controller.js gone). Dangling wiring proof: `grep -rn 'message-composer|message_composer' app/views/` => 3 matches in conversations/_composer.html.erb (lines 3,6,9). `git show 867907a --stat` => deletion of message_composer_controller.js. Boot unaffected; suite stays GREEN: the chat system tests (chat_test.rb) submit via `click_button "Send"` / `click_button "Start chatting"` and never use the Enter path, never assert the 'Sending...' busy text or autofocus; importmap/eagerLoad does not error on the missing file. Fix = `git restore` the file (NOT recreate from scratch).
items.adaptation: SAME as deepseek_v4_1_flash precedent: delete a Stimulus controller that is wired via a kebab-case data-controller (grep-invisible by filename) but never exercised by the suite, so the suite stays green while a real composer behavior silently breaks. deepseek deleted message_form_controller.js (Enter-to-send + resize); minimax's direct analog is message_composer_controller.js (Enter-to-send + autofocus + busy-state). Same class + Med 2. NOTE: chat_scroll_controller.js was NOT chosen (it is the other wired controller); message_composer is the closer behavioral analog to the precedent.
